history.period: 8th-10th century AD (original stone temple); present structure rebuilt early 20th century
history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple on a hillock on the northern side of Tezpur. Legend attributes the original stone temple to the asura king Banasura, whose capital was Sonitpur (ancient Tezpur); the lingam is said to be of 'living stone' that grows over the years, and local tradition calls it one of the largest Shiva lingams in Asia. Archaeologists assign the original stone temple to the Salasthambha dynasty, c. 8th-10th century AD (huge broken stone pillars around the complex are its remains). The original structure was destroyed in the medieval period and rebuilt by successive rulers; Ahom kings of the Tungkhungiya line endowed devottar land and appointed pujaris and paiks. The 1897 earthquake heavily damaged the temple; the present concrete structure was rebuilt in the early 20th century by the monk Swayamvara Bharati (Naga Baba), with a Nat Mandir added by Sri Mahadeo Bharati and Ganesha-Hanuman dwarpal images and an ornamental entrance carved by local artist Sri Joy Das. It is now managed by the Government of Assam through a committee headed by the Deputy Commissioner, Sonitpur. CSV state column held the town name ('Tezpur'); corrected to Assam. FLAG: Wikipedia's infobox dates establishment to the 18th century, conflicting with the 8th-10th century Salasthambha attribution used by archaeologists and other sources.

name: Mahabhairav Temple
town_description: Tezpur, on the north bank of the Brahmaputra in Sonitpur district, is one of Assam's oldest towns, associated in legend with Banasura's capital Sonitpur and with a cluster of ancient temples and ruins (Mahabhairav, Bhairabi, Agnigarh). It is a cultural and educational centre of Upper Assam.

travel.road: Well connected by road to Guwahati and other North Assam towns; the temple sits on a hillock in the northern part of town

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri (February/March) draws large crowds
